Here is a revised version that weaves Donivan’s schooling and faith in more naturally throughout the note, so it feels organic and conversational rather than like a standalone update.

:::writing{id="73922" variant="email" subject="Thank You for Your Kindness and Care"}
Dear Skip,

Thank you so much for reaching out and for the care and intention behind your message. We truly feel so blessed to be part of this community. God very clearly placed us here at exactly the right time, and the love, faith, and support around us have been a steady source of comfort during a season that has not been easy.

I also wanted to share that my divorce is almost final, and most importantly, we are safe and healing after leaving an abusive relationship. Knowing we are surrounded by people who genuinely care has brought a level of peace I cannot fully put into words.

One of the greatest gifts through all of this has been watching my son grow in his faith. He is now attending a classical Christian school, and being immersed in Scripture, structure, and strong values has grounded him in such a beautiful way. His relationship with the Lord has grown so much, and honestly, it has strengthened my own faith right alongside his. Seeing God work so clearly through him has been one of the anchors keeping us steady.

Thank you for sharing the information about Stephen Ministry and for explaining it so thoughtfully. I really appreciate how you framed it as an option and a support, without pressure. Knowing that kind of resource exists, especially during hard seasons like this, is incredibly meaningful, and I will absolutely reach out if and when it feels like the right next step.

Please also extend my gratitude to Kathy. Knowing we are being prayed for and supported in this way means more than you know. We feel very grateful to be here and to be surrounded by such a loving, faith filled community.

With sincere thanks,  
Bethany

Here is a warm, gracious, faith centered reply you can send to Skip. It acknowledges his care, reassures him, and keeps the tone sincere and appreciative without oversharing.

:::writing{id="73921" variant="email" subject="Thank You for Your Kindness and Care"}
Dear Skip,

Thank you so much for taking the time to reach out and for the incredible thoughtfulness in your message. Please know how deeply grateful we are for you and for this community. We truly feel God placed us right here at exactly the right time, and being surrounded by such a loving, faith filled neighborhood has been an unexpected blessing during a very difficult season.

I also want to share that my divorce is almost final, and most importantly, we are safe and healing after leaving an abusive relationship. That alone feels like a miracle, and I am so thankful for God’s protection and provision through it all.

My son is now attending a classical Christian school, and his walk with the Lord has become incredibly strong. His faith has been such a rock for him, and honestly for me as well. Watching God work through his life has brought me so much peace and reassurance.

Thank you for sharing information about Stephen Ministry and for explaining it so thoughtfully. I truly appreciate you offering this resource, and I will absolutely reach out if and when it feels like the right step during these hard times. It means more than you know to have someone extend that kind of care without pressure, expectation, or agenda.

Please also thank Kathy for me. Knowing we are being prayed for and supported in this way is a comfort beyond words. We feel very blessed to be part of this community and to know neighbors like you.

With sincere gratitude,  
Bethany

Tell him my divorce is almost final and that we are safe from that abusive relationship. My son is being raising in a classical Christian school wherr he is super strong with the Lord and its ,been my rock as well. Thank him for this info and I'll definitely reach out to them during these hard times. : here is his email: Dear Bethany,
First, I’m glad you are in our community, and I regret the trauma your family is experiencing. While I’m hesitant to reach out because you don’t know me well, from our few conversations, I sense a desire to help. (It’s the pastor side that is still in me.) That’s why I reached out this afternoon when I saw you.
 
I mentioned the Stephen Ministry as a possibility. As I said this afternoon, it consists of volunteers who’ve been trained to listen, enabling you to talk through issues with someone that you will not know beforehand, who is not family, your best friend, acquaintance, etc. People you know tend not to be as objective. Everything is confidential. As I said this afternoon, unless you tell me, I will not know that you will even have a Stephen Minister, and if you do tell me you got one, I won’t know who that Stephen Minister is unless you tell me. Also, I will never ask who your Stephen Minister is. All I’m doing is offering you the option. 
 
Also, as I mentioned, the training I received to be a Stephen Minister is far superior to any other counseling or pastoral care training I ever received. Plus, having a Stephen Minister costs nothing except your time and your willingness to be vulnerable. 
 
If you have a Stephen Minister, the usual practice is to meet with this person once a week for an hour (illnesses, work, trips, etc. will cause times to skip meetings, but these are extremely rare). The two of you will choose a place that works best for you. You’ll share what the issue(s) are that led you to seek a Stephen Minister and your personal goals. The two of you will focus on your issues. From time to time, you’ll check with each other to evaluate how it’s going. 
 
What Stephen Ministry is not: therapy, counseling, time to hang out, friendship (although many become friends afterward), etc. 
 
If you want a Stephen Minister, call Sheryl Davis, our Stephen Leader, and tell her I recommended you to talk with her. She’ll set a time with you to meet and get an idea of your situation, so she can pick a person who can best relate to your issue(s). She is absolutely amazing at putting people together. Women are placed with women and men with men.
 
You can reach Sheryl at 931.378.0824. 
 
Also, Stephen Ministry was developed by Dr. Kenneth Haugk, a Lutheran pastor who realized the need for such a ministry for people who care about those who need someone to simply listen to them, who could be more objective than people who know the care receivers, and it would be free.
 
You can Google “Stephen Ministry” to learn more. You’ll find over 14,000 congregations worldwide, from ALL denominations and non-denominations, using this ministry. I’m involved with the one at Brentwood United Methodist Church on Franklin Road, which is the congregation Kathy and I attend. (Right, you do not have to attend Brentwood UMC to have a Stephen Minister, and no one will try to get you to attend BUMC.) 
 
If you want to see more, follow this link to our church website:
[https://bumc.net/care/stephen/](https://bumc.net/care/stephen/)
 
In the brief video, you’ll see Pastor Casey Orr. She’s one of the many pastors we have at Brentwood UMC. Davis Chappell is our lead pastor. They are remarkable pastors. Also, if you want to talk with a pastor, while all of them are great, this is Casey’s primary responsibility.
 
If you have any other questions, feel free to call.
 
Now, let me mention Chrysalis for your son…I believe he’s Donivan. I attended a new weekend retreat for adults called The Walk to Emmaus in 1981, a ministry with a Roman Catholic background that has been rewritten for all denominations by our United Methodist Internal Upper Room Ministries. Its focus is to help feel, see, and experience the presence of God’s loving help in the midst of whatever is going on in our lives.
 
Immediately after my “walk,” because of my expertise in youth ministry, the leaders enlisted me to help develop a youth Walk to Emmaus, which we call Chrysalis. In the end, one other person and I wrote all the original program over a 3-year period, which officially began in 1984. It’s for youth/younger ages 14-24, so both boys at your place can attend. While on the same weekend and in the same large group, high school youth are grouped with high school youth, and the older ones are grouped with each other for all discussions.
 
This ministry spread like wildfire worldwide overnight. Before the 2020 COVID pandemic, there were 50-60 Emmaus and another 10-20 Chrysalis retreats every weekend somewhere in the world. (I don’t know what the number of weekend retreats is these days.) Participants must have sponsors because on weekends, all phones, computers, watches, etc., are put away, enabling participants to focus on being in the moment without distractions. The primary reason for a sponsor is that if your son is on the Chrysalis retreat and an emergency arises, you’d reach me, and then I’ll contact the one person on the weekend who’ll connect him with you. I’ve sponsored over 200 people who went on Emmaus Walks and Chrysalis Flights, and not one person needed to be contacted, missed an important text, email, or call, or experienced a crisis. 
 
Even better, EVERY single person came away from their weekend experience with an indescribable “high.” On my weekend, I didn’t get that “burning bush” type experience, but it did give me a great time to think through some things, and refocus & reset my priorities. 
 
I’ve attached a document I created for youth leaders and pastors to help further explain Chrysalis to their youth. Also, if your “men” want to participate in Chrysalis, it’s this January 17 (8 am) through 19 (5 pm) – one week from this coming Saturday. There is no school on that Monday because of the Martin Luther King Jr. holiday weekend. 
 
If you ever want to try the Walk to Emmaus, the next Women’s Walk to Emmaus in this area is Thursday night (7 pm), April 30 through Sunday, May 3 (6 pm). There’s more I can tell you about Emmaus and Chrysalis if Donivan or you are interested. I am willing to be your sponsor if any or all of you attend wish to attend. As a sponsor, I choose to pay the registration fee because it gives me an awesome “high” to see the joy that emerges from those I’ve sponsored during the weekend (and to know others were helped through Stephen Ministry).  
 
Yes, I’m mentioning Chrysalis and Emmaus because I thought (just a hunch) that you all could use a boost of joy. I need to add that Chrysalis, Emmaus, and Stephen Ministries are three of the most non-threatening, non-manipulating, and uplifting experiences I’ve been a part of in 56 years of ministry.
 
If you are not interested, that’s fine. My feelings won’t be hurt. All I’m doing is offering something that might help during this time in your lives. Kathy and I are still here for you all.
 
 
I just realized I probably typed more than you want to know. If I did, my bad. It's just that I've seen so many lives strengthen through these ministries, and don't want people to miss out.
 
Whatever you do, you are in our prayers.
 
Bless you,
 
Skip Armistead
